espace-deals.meta-title: Espace Deals: WooCommerce e-commerce case study
espace-deals.meta-description: WooCommerce case study: keyword research, site structure, CSV catalogue import, product pages, on-page SEO, cash on delivery and GA4 tracking.
espace-deals.og-title: Espace Deals case study, a WooCommerce store
espace-deals.og-description: From keyword research to order tracking: how I built a complete WooCommerce store for the Tunisian market.
espace-deals.hero-h1: Espace Deals, a WooCommerce store from A to Z.
espace-deals.hero-lead: I built Espace Deals, a store selling kitchen preparation tools for the Tunisian market: keyword research, site structure, catalogue, product pages, on-page SEO, payment and shipping, then tracking of carts and orders.
espace-deals.fact-role-dd: Planned and built the whole store
espace-deals.fact-stack-dd: WordPress, WooCommerce, Kadence theme, Rank Math
espace-deals.fact-market-dd: Tunisia, prices in TND, cash on delivery
espace-deals.demo-p: Espace Deals is a complete store, built to show my method. Products and prices are realistic, but orders are not processed. Product images are free-licence photos (Unsplash, Pexels).
espace-deals.toc-9: What I learned, and what’s next
espace-deals.s1-h2: A complete store, to show the whole job.
espace-deals.s1-line: Espace Deals sells kitchen preparation tools for the Tunisian market. I started on 23 September 2026 and finished in October 2026. The goal: cover the whole job of an e-commerce specialist, from keyword research to order tracking.
espace-deals.s1-beat-1-p: Vegetable cutters and mandolines, choppers and garlic presses, cutting boards, kitchen accessories. 20 products.
espace-deals.s1-beat-2-p: Tunisia: prices in TND, home delivery and cash on delivery.
espace-deals.s1-beat-3-p: A consistent, checked store, built with the method I would use on a real one.
espace-deals.s1-build-1: Local first. Built and tested locally with LocalWP; going online is planned.
espace-deals.s1-build-2: WordPress, WooCommerce and the Kadence theme. I imported a starter template, then removed all of its demo content (products, reviews, pages, menus) and translated its English texts.
espace-deals.s1-build-3: Permalinks set before any content, so the URLs in the plan were fixed from the start.
espace-deals.s1-ai: I used AI tools (Claude Code, Claude Design, Cowork). Every piece of generated content was checked and edited by me.
espace-deals.s2-h2: 54 keywords, each tied to one page.
espace-deals.s2-line: I looked for the keywords shoppers actually type, using Google autocomplete in Tunisia, then organised them in Google Sheets. For each keyword: type, intent, target page, role (main or secondary) and priority.
espace-deals.s2-fig-excluded: 33brand and store suggestions excluded, each with its reason
espace-deals.s2-rule-2: Precise keyword with an attribute → product page.
espace-deals.s2-rule-4: One main keyword per page, checked by a formula in the sheet, to avoid cannibalisation.
espace-deals.s2-changed-1-h: “planche à découper inox” (stainless steel cutting board)
espace-deals.s2-changed-1-p: The research showed strong demand for this keyword in Tunisia, so I changed the product range.
espace-deals.s2-changed-2-p: I dropped this weak category name after checking it in Google.
espace-deals.s2-shot-alt: Espace Deals keyword sheet in Google Sheets: keyword, type, intent, target page, role and priority
espace-deals.s2-shot-caption: Google Sheets: the keyword sheet, one row per keyword with its target page.
espace-deals.s3-h2: 26 pages in the plan, all within 3 clicks.
espace-deals.s3-line: Before creating a single product, I wrote the URL plan: 5 categories, 20 products and 1 guide (planned). Every page is at most 3 clicks from the home page.
espace-deals.s3-permalinks: Permalinks were set before adding any content.
espace-deals.s4-line: I built the catalogue in a spreadsheet, then imported it into WooCommerce by CSV. Each product arrives with its SKU, category, attributes, price and stock status.
espace-deals.s4-table-caption: What every product in the catalogue contains
espace-deals.s4-row-attr-td: “Matière” (material) as a global attribute, used for filters; “Contenance / Dimensions” (capacity / size).
espace-deals.s4-row-desc-td: A unique short and long description for every product.
espace-deals.s4-row-stock-td: Stock status set for every product.
espace-deals.s4-row-promo-td: One scheduled promotion, with a start date and an end date.
espace-deals.s4-quality-h3: Data quality and consistency before import
espace-deals.s4-quality-p: Before the import, I checked separators, units and categories. I fixed two problems: commas inside attribute values, and unit formats.
espace-deals.s4-shot-alt: Espace Deals product list in WooCommerce: SKU, price, stock and category
espace-deals.s4-shot-caption: The catalogue in WooCommerce: 20 products with SKU, price, stock and category
espace-deals.s5-h2: Unique product pages, written from the keywords.
espace-deals.s5-line: Every product page and category page follows the keyword sheet: one main keyword, an SEO title, a meta description and links to neighbouring pages.
espace-deals.s5-pages-1: Unique descriptions. A short and a long description for each of the 20 products, with its specifications.
espace-deals.s5-pages-2: Product photos: free-licence photos (Unsplash, Pexels) for all 20 products.
espace-deals.s5-seo-1: SEO title and meta description for the home page, the 5 categories and the 20 product pages, written from the keyword sheet.
espace-deals.s5-seo-3: Clean H1 and H2 on every page.
espace-deals.s5-seo-4: Internal links between categories and products; breadcrumbs and an XML sitemap.
espace-deals.s5-seo-5: Structured data: Product / Offer (JSON-LD) on the product pages, validated in Google’s Rich Results Test.
espace-deals.s5-shot-rankmath-alt: Rank Math on the Râpe 4 faces inox product: Google preview with SEO title and meta description, focus keyword, score 85/100
espace-deals.s5-shot-rankmath-caption: Rank Math on the “Râpe 4 faces inox” product: SEO title, meta description and a score of 85/100.
espace-deals.s5-shot-rich-alt: Google Rich Results Test: Product snippets and Merchant listings, 2 valid items detected
espace-deals.s5-shot-rich-caption: Google Rich Results Test on the product page code (the store is still local): Product snippets and Merchant listings valid, with non-critical warnings.
espace-deals.s6-h2: Cash on delivery, free shipping from 150 DT.
espace-deals.s6-line: I set the store up for Tunisian buying habits: prices in dinars, cash on delivery and clear shipping costs.
espace-deals.s6-pay-1: TND currency with 3 decimals, plus a small PHP snippet (Code Snippets plugin) to display “DT”.
espace-deals.s6-pay-2: Tunisia shipping zone: home delivery at 7 DT, free from 150 DT to encourage a higher average order value.
espace-deals.s6-pay-3: Cash on delivery as the payment method, matching Tunisian buying habits.
espace-deals.s6-site-1: Home page and header in French: hero, featured categories and products, reassurance bar (cash on delivery, 7 DT delivery / free from 150 DT, returns) and my own logo.
espace-deals.s6-site-2: Information pages: Delivery, Returns, About, and Contact.
espace-deals.s6-site-3: “Demo store” notice on every page and at checkout.
espace-deals.s6-site-4: A complete test order with cash on delivery, from product page to confirmation.
espace-deals.s6-shot-shipping-alt: WooCommerce settings: Tunisia shipping zone with home delivery and free delivery
espace-deals.s6-shot-shipping-caption: WooCommerce: Tunisia shipping zone, home delivery at 7 DT and free delivery from 150 DT.
espace-deals.s6-shot-order-alt: Confirmation page of test order #1277 on Espace Deals, cash on delivery
espace-deals.s6-shot-order-caption: Test order #1277: confirmation page, cash on delivery.
espace-deals.s7-h2: The buying journey, measured step by step.
espace-deals.s7-line: I set up GA4 with Google Tag Manager (GTM4WP plugin) to track carts and orders. Each step of the buying journey sends its e-commerce event.
espace-deals.s7-checked: I checked every event in Google Tag Manager Preview mode and in GA4 DebugView.
espace-deals.s7-shot-ga4-alt: GA4 DebugView during a test purchase: view_item_list, add_payment_info, add_shipping_info and purchase events
espace-deals.s7-shot-ga4-caption: GA4 DebugView during a test purchase (GA4 + Google Tag Manager + GTM4WP).
espace-deals.s8-h2: The store, from the shopper’s side.
espace-deals.s8-line: The home page, a category page with its filters and a product page: what a shopper sees.
espace-deals.s8-shot-home-alt: Espace Deals home page in French
espace-deals.s8-shot-home-caption: Home page: hero, featured categories and products, reassurance bar.
espace-deals.s8-shot-cat-alt: Espace Deals category page with filters by material
espace-deals.s8-shot-cat-caption: Category page: intro text and filters by material.
espace-deals.s8-shot-product-alt: Espace Deals product page: image, price in DT, description and specifications
espace-deals.s8-shot-product-caption: Product page: image, price in DT, descriptions and specifications.
espace-deals.s9-h2: What I learned, and what I would do next.
espace-deals.s9-learned-1: Keyword research shapes the offer too, not just the copy: “planche à découper inox” changed the product range.
espace-deals.s9-learned-2: Fix the data before the import. One comma inside an attribute value is enough to break a CSV row.
espace-deals.s9-learned-3: Structure comes before content: URL plan and permalinks first, product pages second.
espace-deals.s9-learned-4: AI speeds things up, but it does not validate. Every generated text has to be read and edited.
espace-deals.s9-next-intro: My recommendations if the store carried on:
espace-deals.s9-next-1: Put the store online, verify the domain in Google Search Console and submit the XML sitemap.
espace-deals.s9-next-2: Connect the catalogue to Meta (Meta for WooCommerce) to sell on Facebook and Instagram.
espace-deals.s9-next-3: Read the Search Console queries to improve product page titles and descriptions.
espace-deals.s9-next-4: Add more guides based on the questions found in the keyword sheet.
espace-deals.s9-next-5: Test a marketplace listing for part of the catalogue.
espace-deals.s9-pagenav: %CV_LABEL_LONG% Email me Back to home

worku.meta-title: Worku: launching and repositioning a B2B product
worku.meta-description: Worku, a B2B sourcing SaaS: the pivot from ATS to sourcing, positioning, audience journeys, prospecting, customer research and LinkedIn content.
worku.og-title: Worku: launching and repositioning a B2B product
worku.og-description: My experience as co-founder and digital marketing officer on a B2B SaaS, from an applicant tracker to a sourcing platform.
worku.hero-h1: Worku: launching and repositioning a B2B product.
worku.hero-lead: Worku is a B2B SaaS platform that finds professional profiles and returns verified contact details for recruiters and sales teams. I’m a co-founder, with two partners, and I was its digital marketing officer, working directly with the CTO, from August 2025 to September 2026.
worku.beat-1-p: A sourcing platform: you describe the person you need, Worku returns their profile and verified contact details.
worku.beat-2-p: Digital Marketing Officer and co-founder, with two partners. Working directly with the CTO.
worku.beat-3-p: My Master’s internship (Feb–Jul 2026) was part of this role.
worku.h2-we-built-the-wrong-product: We built the wrong product first.
worku.p-worku-has-existed-in-two: Worku has existed in two versions. This is how it got from one to the other.
worku.p-recruiters-posted-a-job-an: Recruiters posted a job. An AI scored whoever applied.
worku.p-it-stayed-live-for-more: It stayed live for more than six months. The model never took hold.
worku.p-we-went-to-recruiters-and: We went to recruiters and asked what they actually needed instead.
worku.p-millions-of-profiles-searchable-return: Millions of profiles, searchable, returned with verified contact details.
worku.p-live-for-more-than-six: Live for more than six months
worku.span-and-fills-it-in-cv: And fills it inCV, portfolio, and questions about their career, projects and experience.
worku.p-every-step-waited-on-the: Every step waited on the right person deciding to apply.
worku.span-a-recruiter-describes-who-they: A recruiter describes who they needIn plain language. No job posting.
worku.span-the-search-runs-across-millions: The search runs across millions of profiles
worku.p-the-recruiter-goes-to-the: The recruiter goes to the person, instead of waiting for them.
worku.scope-team-2: The data: contact enrichment and verification
worku.scope-me-1: Positioning and messaging after the pivot
worku.scope-me-3: Customer research (ICP, personas) and competitor analysis
worku.scope-ai: The page mock-ups and code were produced with Claude Code and Claude Design under my direction; I checked every change before it went live.
worku.prospect-1: A tracking file in Google Sheets. 200+ prospects, each with type, specialty, LinkedIn activity, a score, a status, the next action and notes.
worku.prospect-2: Contact enrichment with Worku, FullEnrich, Prospeo and ContactOut.
worku.prospect-3: Outreach messages and follow-ups written by me; results shared with the co-founders.
worku.prospect-mock-caption: Mock example: the structure of the file, with no real data.
worku.research-line: Before rewriting a page I mapped the two audiences and the vocabulary each one uses.
worku.research-1: ICP and persona research. Separated the recruiter buyer from the sales buyer, since they search with different words.
worku.research-2: Competitor analysis. Studied how comparable sourcing tools position and price themselves.
worku.research-3: Product testing. Used the sourcing tool as a user, documented relevance and filtering issues, and fed them back to the technical team.
worku.message-h2: From what it is, to what you get.
worku.caption-homepage-message-before-and-afte: Homepage message, before and after. The “after” is live on worku.tn.
worku.td-d-crivez-le-d-cideur: Décrivez le décideur. Obtenez ses coordonnées vérifiées.
worku.alt-screen-recording-of-the-restructured: Screen recording of the restructured Worku homepage
worku.p-worku-tn-after-the-restructure: worku.tn after the restructure. H1: “Décrivez le décideur. Obtenez ses coordonnées vérifiées.” Primary call to action: “Lancer une recherche gratuite.” Recorded 2026.
worku.alt-the-worku-homepage-as-it: The Worku homepage as it loads today at 1440 by 900, captured from the live site. Above the fold: the headline Decrivez le decideur, obtenez ses coordonnees verifiees, one explanatory sentence, a blue button reading Lancer une recherche gratuite and a secondary button Voir comment ca marche, with the product interface alongside.
worku.caption-live-worku-tn-at-1440: Live worku.tn at 1440×900, September 2026. Everything the argument needs is above the fold: the H1 names the task, and the button directly under it names the next step.
worku.linkedin-h2: Four pillars, every post picks one.
worku.linkedin-line: I set the editorial line for Worku’s LinkedIn company page and published about 9 posts between February and July 2026, organic only. Each post picks one pillar.
worku.li-start-from-a-real-problem: Start from a real problem. Open on something the reader recognises from their own week, not on the product.
worku.li-show-the-product-in-use: Show the product in use. Concrete, in context, doing the job.
worku.li-speak-to-one-audience-a: Speak to one audience. A recruiter post is not a sales post. Never both at once.
worku.li-explain-the-product-s-evolution: Explain the product’s evolution. Make the move from applicant tracking to sourcing legible.
worku.alt-a-five-page-carousel-post-published: A five-page carousel post published by the Worku company page on LinkedIn, opening on the slide “On était silencieux, le produit lui travaillait”
worku.caption-linkedin-worku-company-page-june: LinkedIn, Worku company page, June 2026. A five-page carousel: it opens on the problem (no tool gives a specific profile’s contact details), then shows a profile search. Published by the page.
worku.alt-a-linkedin-post-on-the: A LinkedIn post on the Worku company page beginning Six months ago, Worku was an ATS, followed by a before and after graphic titled Trouver, Verifier, Contacter
worku.caption-linkedin-worku-company-page-six: LinkedIn, Worku company page. “Six months ago, Worku was an ATS…” The pivot from applicant tracking to sourcing, told with the before and after. Pillar: explain the product’s evolution.
worku.alt-a-linkedin-post-on-the--2: A LinkedIn post on the Worku company page with the headline Trouvez vos prochains talents avant vos concurrents, showing a natural-language search returning a verified developer profile
worku.caption-linkedin-worku-company-page-trou: LinkedIn, Worku company page. “Trouvez vos prochains talents… avant vos concurrents.” A recruiter-facing search demo. Pillar: speak to one audience.
worku.lessons-eyebrow: What it taught me for e-commerce
worku.lessons-h2: Four habits that carry over to a store.
worku.lessons-1: Write for one specific buyer: the same product is described with different words depending on the customer.
worku.lessons-2: A button should say what happens after the click.
worku.lessons-3: Separate the journeys when customers don’t have the same needs, like category pages.
worku.lessons-4: Test the product as a customer before promoting it.
worku.limits-h3: What this page does not claim
worku.limits-1: No traffic, conversion or audience-growth claim. I have no reliable measurement to show, so I don’t claim any.
worku.limits-2: The changes are verifiable, their impact is not. The message and the pages are live on worku.tn; their effect has not been measured.

ux-ui.meta-title: UX/UI: customer journeys and interfaces | Louai Bouraoui
ux-ui.meta-description: Journey audit, wireframes, message before/after, audience pages and mobile on the Worku SaaS, then two Tuni’AR apps, one of them a shop.
ux-ui.og-description: Finding where a journey loses the visitor, then clearing the path to the action.
ux-ui.hero-lead: I find where a journey loses the visitor, then I clear the path to the action. It’s the same logic as a buying journey.
ux-ui.hero-context: Sections 01 to 05: the website of the Worku SaaS, in 2026. Then two mobile apps designed during my Tuni’AR internship, in 2024.
ux-ui.p-i-mapped-the-five-stages: I mapped the five stages a visitor passes through, then marked where each one loses them.
ux-ui.alt-my-user-journey-audit-of-worku: My user-journey audit of Worku, in French. A verdict bar reads a modern, coherent visual base but an insufficiently structured and guided experience. Five numbered stages run left to right: arrival on the homepage, understanding the service, identifying the need, discovering how it works, and taking action. Each carries a flagged friction. Two cross-cutting problems follow, information hierarchy and mobile experience, above a dark bar reading higher comprehension effort, hesitation, extra navigation, risk of abandonment.
ux-ui.caption-user-journey-audit-worku-five-st: User-journey audit, Worku. Five stages, friction flagged at each. February 2026.
ux-ui.li-unclear-entry-the-first-screen: Unclear entryThe first screen spoke to everyone, so it spoke to no one.
ux-ui.li-no-segmentation-recruiters-and-sales: No segmentationRecruiters and sales teams shared one path.
ux-ui.li-undemonstrated-product-the-four-steps: Undemonstrated productThe four steps of the product were never shown in order.
ux-ui.li-vague-actions-commencer-maintenant-di: Vague actionsCommencer maintenant didn’t say what happened next.
ux-ui.p-before-choosing-a-colour-i: Before choosing a colour, I settled what goes where and in what order.

ux-ui.caption-the-same-page-at-390: The same page at 390. Fourteen sections, one column — scroll the frame to walk it end to end.

ux-ui.alt-the-worku-homepage-before-the: The Worku homepage before the redesign: a badge and a headline built around the “AI sourcing” category, a paragraph about the platform and a blue “Commencer maintenant” button. A quick-search card on the right.

ux-ui.h2-a-recruiter-and-a-sales: A recruiter and a sales rep are not the same visitor.
ux-ui.p-they-arrive-with-different-words: They arrive with different words and different jobs. One page could not serve both, so I built four.
ux-ui.p-4-dedicated-pages-up-from: 4dedicated pages, up from one general page
